title: Field notes: Console experiments & rollout hitchhikes - 2026-04-10
content:
Purpose: quick, lightweight capture from the Monday field discussion — trying to surface small unknowns that are tripping canaries and the mobile UI experiment.

Attendees (ad hoc): Anika, Marcus, Priya, Diego, Sara (ops), Julian (data).
Context: last week's canary (alpha routing -> v2 telemetry) showed a 7% elevation in error traces for the analytics ingestion path and a subtle layout jitter seen in mobile web when switching between conversation and history. We ran a narrow canary (10% traffic) and rolled it back at 0300 UTC. This doc captures threads and concrete follow-ups.

What we observed (raw):
- Analytics: incoming event amplify between service:analytics-consumer and the telemetry-insert lambda. Error class: transient HTTP 502 from the internal gateway; spike aligns with peaks of batched uploads.
- UI (mobile): when history panel is expanded while streaming messages are appended, a reflow triggers CSS repaint; perceived as a 120–180ms flicker on some Safari mobile versions. Not reproducible in emulator with throttled CPU consistently.
- Rollouts: the A/B rule that pins traffic by cookie had an edge-case when users clear cookies mid-session; our session-affinity fallback was sending them back to the older variant but with a v2 feature toggle enabled leading to mixed-state UI.

Hypotheses / quick checks:
- Hypothesis 1 (analytics): the consumer batching window is slightly larger under low throughput which makes occasional oversized payloads trip the gateway timeout; check batch size distribution and compare with gateway limits.
- Hypothesis 2 (analytics): a recent change to compression headers (PR 482) introduced a client-side header ordering difference that some legacy proxies mishandle. Validate with raw packet capture on a canary route.
- Hypothesis 3 (UI jitter): CSS contains an absolute-to-relative layout switch when history toggles; animation uses 'height: auto' fallback which is notoriously slow on iOS Safari. Replace with transform-based animation to test.
- Hypothesis 4 (rollouts): cookie clearing + rollout policy mismatch is a design gap; we should make the fallback deterministic by consulting the routing control-plane before serving any new feature flags for the session.

Action items (owners + short due dates):
- Marcus: extract batch size histogram for analytics-consumer over last 72h and annotate windows with 502 spikes. (due: 2026-04-12)
- Priya: run headless mobile Safari harness with the history toggle at 2x streaming rate to force reflow; capture timeline traces and upload flamegraph. If repro, prototype transform animation. (due: 2026-04-13)
- Diego: deploy a tiny canary variant that keeps previous compression header ordering to 2% traffic for 48h and monitor error trends; link metrics into the canary dashboard. (due: 2026-04-11)
- Anika: update rollout policy doc snippet to require routing-control-plane sync after cookie loss and prepare a minimal rollback-runbook update. (due: 2026-04-14)
- Julian (data): add a derived metric: "batched_payload_size_p90" and correlate with gateway_502_count; surface as annotation in rollout dashboard. (due: 2026-04-12)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we accept a short-term guardrail of limiting batch_size to 90th percentile prior to a deeper fix? (ops/infra sign-off required)
- Should we opt for animation change in the upcoming UI sprint (risk: other browsers might need tweak) or keep current and hide history toggle on mobile for the short term? (product tradeoff)

Notes on experiment design:
- Canary split should be sticky by user-id when available; cookie-based affinity is secondary. Need to validate telemetry has user-id for >95% of active sessions before we migrate split logic.
- For the compression header experiment, add a header x-experiment:compress-reorder so we can query logs easily.

Quick checklist for the rollback path (for on-call):
- Toggle route-back to v1 via hot-route switch (infra api) -> expected <3s propagation.
- Disable compression reorder flag at edge (edge config) if rollback triggered.
- Run small smoke pipeline: simulate 500 batched events and verify gateway returns 200s.

Resources / references:
- Related PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482 (compression reorder), github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/487 (history toggle minor refactor).
- Jira tickets: ENG-1729 (analytics 502 spike), ENG-1741 (mobile history jitter).
- Slack threads: #console-rollouts (links posted at 2026-04-09 22:04), #infra-gateway (trace posted by Sara).

Retrospective note (call it out):
- The rollout checklist works for giant regressions but small, compositional edge cases (cookie + feature-toggle mix) are still not well-covered. We should add a new 'cookie-loss' test to the rollout smoke suite. Low-effort test, high ROI.

Meeting wrap (raw next steps):
- Quick sync Wednesday 11:00 PT to check early signals (15m).
- If Diego's 2% canary shows reduction in 48h, plan staged rollout around 2026-04-16 with infra windows.

Loose thoughts / to-self section (informal):
- If we move animation to transforms, remember to test with reduced-motion accessibility setting.
- Consider adding an observability tag when a user clears cookie (we already surface 'session_start' but not 'session_repair').
- Think about a canary scoring metric that factors both user-visible errors and backend ingestion health; raw error count alone is noisy.

-- end --
